These examples introduce the main exercise controls: one or several answer
fields, required answer forms, text answers, partial credit, collapsible tasks,
and pools of alternative questions.

## A single answer field

```{math-exercise}
#| label: basic-single
What is $7\cdot 6$? _[42]
```

The expression inside the brackets is the expected answer. It is not shown to
the student in the rendered page.

## Answer fields of different widths

```{math-exercise}
#| label: basic-widths
#| field-labels: Short answer, Medium answer, Long answer
Short: _[2]

Medium: __[123456]

Long mathematical expression: ___[(1+2+3+4+5)^2]
```

## A collapsible exercise

```{math-exercise}
#| label: basic-caption
#| caption: Click this heading to open the exercise
Compute $5^2$: _[25]
```

## Multiple fields and meaningful labels

```{math-exercise}
#| label: basic-labels
#| field-labels: Sum, Product, Difference
#| partial-credit: true
For the numbers $7$ and $3$, enter their sum _[10], product _[21], and
difference _[4].
```

## Requiring a particular form

```{math-exercise}
#| label: basic-factored
#| caption: Equivalent is not enough when a form is requested
#| vars: x
#| form: factored
Factor $x^2+5x+6$: __[(x+2)*(x+3)]
```

## Case-insensitive text

```{math-exercise}
#| label: basic-text
#| mode: string_ci
Write the conventional name of the constant $\pi$: __[pi]
```

## A random task pool

The selected task is stable during a browser session. Use the reload button in
the corner to request another variant.

```{math-exercise}
#| label: basic-pool
#| caption: Random arithmetic task
#| pool: true

$8+7=$ _[15]

---

$9\cdot6=$ _[54]

---

$2^8=$ _[256]
```

## Rejecting a specific unfinished form

```{math-exercise}
#| label: basic-reject
#| vars: x
#| reject: (x+1)^2
Expand $(x+1)^2$: __[x^2+2*x+1]
```
